Veterans Day is Wednesday, Nov. 11 — and across Laredo, restaurants are saying thank you the way this city knows best: with a free meal.

The best-known offer is at Texas Roadhouse, which will distribute free meal vouchers to veterans and active-duty U.S. military members on Wednesday from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at every location, including Laredo's at 5722 San Bernardo Ave. Guests must show proof of service, such as a military or VA card or discharge papers.

The voucher covers a choice of 10 entrées — including a 6-ounce sirloin — along with two made-from-scratch sides and a Coca-Cola product, sweet tea, iced tea, or coffee. It can be redeemed for dine-in or carry-out from dinner service on Veterans Day, or any time through May 31, 2027. This is the 17th annual edition of Texas Roadhouse's “Texas-size Thank You for Serving Our Country” event, at close to 700 restaurants nationwide.

More free meals around town

Texas Roadhouse is not the only table. Red Lobster is offering a free Veteran's Shrimp & Chips — six Walt's Favorite Shrimp with cocktail sauce, French fries and coleslaw — on Nov. 11 for veterans, active-duty military and reservists who show a valid military ID, WeSalute+ ID card or proof of service. The offer is dine-in only.

Hacienda Mexican Restaurants will honor veterans and active-duty military with a free large wet burrito when they dine in or carry out on Nov. 11, with proof of service. The offer covers active duty, military retirees, veterans, Reserve and National Guard members, and dependents.

Other chains across Texas are running Veterans Day offers as well, including free meals at Bombshells, Cotton Patch Cafe, Chili's and Golden Corral, according to a statewide roundup verified through Nov. 4. Veterans should check with each restaurant before going, since hours and terms can vary by location.

Parades and ceremonies

Texas' major Veterans Day parades run Wednesday in Houston (American Heroes Parade, 11:30 a.m.), Fort Worth (Tarrant County Parade, 11 a.m.) and El Paso (Northeast Parade, 10 a.m. MST). Some Texas communities hold their observances on adjacent weekends, so veterans and families should check dates carefully rather than assuming every event falls on the 11th.

Webb Watch 956 could not verify a Laredo-specific Veterans Day parade or ceremony for Wednesday from public listings reviewed for this story. Veterans looking for local observances can check with the City of Laredo, local veterans organizations, and the Texas Veterans Commission, which provides free claims assistance.
